correctness.rationale: Let X be a real Hilbert-isomorphic Banach space dim>=2, with multiplicative Euclidean distortion d. For every D>d transport a Hilbert norm with r B_H subset B_X subset R B_H and R/r<D. A Hilbert-skew rotation J on a two-dimensional orthonormal subspace satisfies J^2=-P and ||J||_X²>=||P||_X>=1. Riesz representation of each norming pair f(x)=1 and the bound |h||x|<=R/r show |f(Jx)|² <= |h|²|x|²-1 <=D²-1, so n(X)<=sqrt(d²-1) after D downarrow d. For the regular 4m-gon unit ball, cyclic averaging of arbitrary Hilbert quadratic forms proves d_BM=sec(beta), beta=pi/(4m); vertex extreme norming functionals u +/-tan(beta) Ju establish n>=tan(beta), while the quarter-turn has numerical radius tan(beta), giving equality. Thus coefficient 1 and the sqrt2 near-d=1 constant are sharp. Independent finite checks with all 81 integer-entry 2x2 matrices in {-1,0,1}⁴ across regular 4,8,12,16-gons corroborate vertex inequalities; infinite-dimensional and all-operator statements follow from the analytic proof, not these samples.

value.rationale: A sharp explicit stability inequality connecting two fundamental Banach invariants for every real Hilbert-isomorphic space including infinite dimensions, with genuine exact equality witnesses approaching the Hilbert limit, gives an optimal modulus where existing work proved continuity. The known polygon numerical indices are credited; value lies in the simultaneous global inequality and sharp norm-distortion comparison.

limitations: Real scalars and dimension at least 2 essential; for d>=sqrt2 bound can be vacuous; no equality-case classification at every d.
The known regular polygon index is not original, and the finite matrix examples do not prove it.
residual_risks: A less-indexed quantitative numerical-index modulus might imply the square-root inequality; no comprehensive originality certificate.
